Any reference to one of these names resolves against the file listed above. MOVE_TO_INDEX_CONTRACT.value: `buildReorderBodyToIndex(ids, movedId, targetIndex)` returns `{ job_ids }` = `arrayMove(ids, oldIndex, targetIndex)` where `oldIndex = ids.indexOf(movedId)` and `targetIndex` is the FINAL index the moved row must occupy, resolved against the PRE-MOVE array as `targetIndex = ids.indexOf(over.id)` (dnd-kit's standard sortable pattern: both indices are found in the original item array and handed to arrayMove unchanged). The implementation removes then re-inserts, but `targetIndex` is NOT an index into the post-removal array - it is the final index. WORKED EXAMPLES, both mandatory as unit assertions: forward `[A,B,C,D]`, move A over C -> oldIndex 0, targetIndex 2 -> `[B,C,A,D]` (NOT `[B,A,C,D]`); backward `[A,B,C,D]`, move D over B -> oldIndex 3, targetIndex 1 -> `[A,D,B,C]`; adjacent forward `[A,B,C]`, move A over B -> `[B,A,C]`. Out-of-range targetIndex clamps to [0, len-1]. An unknown movedId returns `{ job_ids: [...ids] }` unchanged - the same defensive shape buildReorderBody already uses for an unknown selectedId. targetIndex === current index returns the identity permutation, and the caller MUST NOT issue a PUT for an identity permutation.
MOVE_TO_INDEX_CONTRACT.source: Research-backed - dnd-kit sortable's own arrayMove(items, oldIndex, newIndex) semantics, reconciled with the existing buildReorderBody unknown-id branch (convert-controls.ts:112-118).
MOVE_TO_INDEX_CONTRACT.note: The existing 4-value direction union cannot express an arbitrary drop target, which is why a second builder exists rather than a fifth direction. The earlier wording ('an index into the array after removal') was ambiguous enough to admit `[B,A,C,D]` for the forward example and was corrected in plan review round 1 (F2).

DND_HOVER_REVEAL_RULE.value: "On hover" is implemented as an OPACITY-ONLY reveal: the handle is always mounted, always focusable and always in the accessibility tree; it is `opacity-0` and becomes `opacity-100` on `group-hover:`, `group-focus-within:` and its own `focus-visible:`. It is NEVER `aria-hidden`, NEVER `display:none`, NEVER `hidden`, and its width never animates.
DND_HOVER_REVEAL_RULE.source: Spec - 10-queue-card-ui.md:254 ("on hover") reconciled with G33_RULE (animate transform/opacity only) and WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible.
DND_HOVER_REVEAL_RULE.note: A display-toggled handle is invisible to keyboard and touch users, who are exactly the population WCAG_DRAG_RULE protects. Opacity also keeps layout stable, so no row reflows on hover.

DND_TOUCH_ACTION_RULE.value: The drag handle MUST carry `touch-action: none` (Tailwind `touch-none`). Asserted twice: a unit assertion that the handle className contains `touch-none` and none of `touch-auto`/`touch-pan-y`, and an E2E assertion that `getComputedStyle(handle).touchAction === 'none'` on the rendered Electron page.
DND_TOUCH_ACTION_RULE.source: Research-backed - dnd-kit PointerSensor documentation: under Pointer Events a touch drag inside a scrollable list is claimed by the browser's native scroll gesture unless touch-action is disabled on the activator, and preventDefault on the initiating touchmove is not reliable. dnd-kit recommends touch-action: none on a dedicated activator rather than a TouchSensor + delay constraint.
DND_TOUCH_ACTION_RULE.note: Added in plan review round 1 (F3). Without it the mouse E2E passes while touch drag scrolls the list instead of reordering - a failure the planned pointer driver cannot expose, which is why the contract is asserted structurally (class + computed style) rather than by simulating a touch drag.

DND_SENSOR_CONFIG.value: PointerSensor with `activationConstraint: { distance: 5 }`, plus KeyboardSensor with `coordinateGetter: sortableKeyboardCoordinates`. TouchSensor is NOT configured: PointerSensor covers touch through pointer events, but ONLY in combination with DND_TOUCH_ACTION_RULE on the activator - the two are a single contract and neither ships without the other.
DND_SENSOR_CONFIG.source: Research-backed - dnd-kit docs recommend a distance/delay activation constraint so a click on a control inside a draggable is not stolen by drag activation; `sortableKeyboardCoordinates` is the sortable preset's required coordinate getter.
DND_SENSOR_CONFIG.note: dnd-kit does NOT use the HTML5 drag-and-drop API - it is pointer-events only. That fact is what makes DRAG_STATE_ISOLATION_RULE testable.

DND_AUTOSCROLL_CONFIG.value: DndContext is given `autoScroll={{ threshold: { x: 0, y: 0.05 }, acceleration: 5 }}`. The library default (`threshold {x:0.2,y:0.2}`, `acceleration: 10`) treats the outer fifth of the nearest scroll ancestor as a trigger band; when that ancestor is the page shell's `<main>` and the queue sits at its bottom, a 20px pointer nudge drives `scrollTop` to its maximum before the pointer reaches the next row.
DND_AUTOSCROLL_CONFIG.source: Research-backed - dnd-kit auto-scroller options (`threshold`, `acceleration`) are the documented control surface; issue #1414 records that the relative default is too aggressive on large containers. Measured 2026-09-11: `scrollTop` went 0 -> 100 -> 149 (max) within two 10px pointer steps; after this config, probe PUT body was exactly AC-49.25 (`dl-2,dl-3,dl-1,dl-4`).
DND_AUTOSCROLL_CONFIG.note: Execution-phase correction X3 (with QUEUE_SCROLL_CONTAINER_RULE). This is the pointer half; it cannot reach KeyboardSensor.handleKeyDown's clamp.

QUEUE_SCROLL_CONTAINER_RULE.value: The nearest scroll ancestor dnd-kit measures must be a bounded box whose rows start at its top, not the page shell's `<main>`. Concretely: (1) the page `<section>` carries `h-full min-h-0` so it fills `<main>` and `<main>` stops overflowing; (2) `download-queue-region` / `convert-queue-region` carries `flex-1 min-h-[20rem]`; (3) `overflow-auto` lives on a per-page wrapper around `QueueList` only, NEVER on QueueList `listClasses` (that node is `relative` and is the containing block for the file-drop overlay at `absolute inset-0`; scrolling it parks the overlay in the overflow, and changing `listClasses` also breaches DND_OPT_IN_RULE's byte-for-byte non-drag DOM); (4) the controls above the queue (help card, SABR/task block, add form, status and error banners) sit in ONE `flex min-h-0 flex-col gap-4 overflow-auto` pane, and the summary + processor + toolbar footer sits in ONE `flex shrink-0 flex-col gap-4` wrapper. Clause (4) decides WHICH pane absorbs the column's height deficit. The page column is oversubscribed at the app's own default window, so some pane must yield; with every child at the flex default `shrink: 1` the deficit is split by content height and the queue is squeezed to ~92px, which re-arms the very clamp clauses (1)-(3) exist to disarm. QueueSelectionHeader, BulkActionBar and BulkResultToast stay OUTSIDE the scroller (USER_LOCKS lock 1). KeyboardSensor.handleKeyDown scrolls-and-returns when `canScrollY && clamped !== requested`; for ArrowDown-by-one on a 62px pitch the wrapper clientHeight must be >= ~124px or AC-49.27 stays red one level down.
QUEUE_SCROLL_CONTAINER_RULE.source: Local Canon - measured 2026-09-11 in Electron (MAIN rect 40-739, rows 548-788, all below midpoint 389.5); KeyboardSensor.handleKeyDown in @dnd-kit/core clamps then scrollTo. Human-approved 2026-09-11 (proceed with Opus-refined option 1) and 2026-09-16 (proceed with X4 rather than defer). Re-measured 2026-09-16 after clause (4): downloader scroller clientHeight 280 == scrollHeight 280 and `<main>` 699 == 699, so BOTH ancestors report maxScroll 0, `canScrollY` is false at every level, and an instrumented keyboard drag recorded zero `scrollTo` calls.
QUEUE_SCROLL_CONTAINER_RULE.note: Execution-phase corrections X3 (clauses 1-3) and X4 (clause 4). Not an AC: the post-Red unit assertions in downloader-page.test.ts and convert-page.test.ts lock the class strings so MEU-52 cannot paste the mockup's old §04 string without failing the suite. Phase 11 grouping names this chain as an input, not a subject. Conversely a file drag over the list must not start a row drag.

REORDER_SINGLE_FLIGHT_RULE.value: EVERY queue permutation mutation on a queue - kebab Move up/down/top/bottom, Alt+Arrow, drag drop, and the WHOLE bulk reorder fold - passes through ONE synchronous gate before it reads the current order or builds a body. New module `ui/src/renderer/src/lib/queue/reorder-single-flight.ts` exports TWO things: (1) `createSingleFlight(): { tryAcquire(): boolean; release(): void; readonly held: boolean }`, a closure over a plain boolean (NOT React state); and (2) `acquireQueueReorder(key: ReorderQueueKey): (() => void) | null`, the queue-scoped registry the pages and useQueueBulk actually call - a MODULE-LEVEL Map keyed by REORDER_QUEUE_KEYS holding one createSingleFlight() instance per queue, returning a one-shot release callback on acquire and `null` when that queue's gate is already held. LIFETIME: the registry is module-level, NOT a per-page `useRef`. A route unmount does not cancel an in-flight PUT, so a ref-held gate is destroyed on navigation while the request it was guarding is still on the wire, and the remounted page immediately grants a second permutation computed from a pre-mutation order - exactly the last-write-wins overwrite this rule exists to prevent. Module scope outlives the component; keying by queue keeps the two queues independent. OWNERSHIP OF THE BULK FOLD: `useQueueBulk.moveSelected()` is the only caller that can see the whole fold - bulkReorder's N sequential requests, the single refetch and the selection release all live inside its `run()` closure and `moveSelected` returns `void` (use-queue-bulk.ts:93, :96-107) - so no page-level caller can wrap it from outside. The gate is therefore acquired INSIDE useQueueBulk, which takes a new required `queueKey` option, and released in a `finally` after the refetch. That is why `ui/src/renderer/src/lib/queue/use-queue-bulk.ts` is a modified file of this MEU. CONTRACT: an entry point calls `acquireQueueReorder(key)` FIRST; on `null` it returns immediately without reading `items`, without building a body and without issuing a PUT; on a release callback it proceeds and invokes that callback in a `finally` that runs after the reconcile completes or the request rejects. Feedback while the gate is held is EQUAL across every entry point per REORDER_FEEDBACK_TIER - no path is silently inert. REACTIVE READ SURFACE (round-5, R4-F3): a gate that only exposes tryAcquire/release can be OBEYED by the pages but cannot be RENDERED, so REORDER_FEEDBACK_TIER clause (4) would be unimplementable — nothing tells a mounted card that the queue's gate was taken by some other card's kebab. The module therefore also exports (3) `isQueueReorderHeld(key): boolean` and (4) `subscribeQueueReorder(key, listener): () => void`, which invokes every listener synchronously on each acquire and release. Those two are the external-store pair `useSyncExternalStore` consumes. THE HOOK ITSELF DOES NOT LIVE HERE: `reorder-single-flight.ts` has NO React import, because `download-commands.ts` and `convert-commands.ts` are plain-TS command modules with no React import of their own and they call `acquireQueueReorder` directly - putting `useSyncExternalStore` in the store would drag React into the command layer purely so a component could subscribe. The hook is REORDER_HELD_HOOK, its own tiny module, which is the standard split for this pattern: a framework-free store plus a one-line React binding. `getSnapshot` returns a boolean, so it is referentially stable by construction and cannot cause the infinite re-render loop useSyncExternalStore throws on for freshly-allocated snapshots. Because the store is the same module-level Map the acquire path writes, a component that unmounts and remounts re-subscribes to the LIVE gate state rather than to a fresh false — which is the same reason the registry is module-level in the first place.
REORDER_SINGLE_FLIGHT_RULE.source: Local Canon - forced by REORDER_WIRE_CONTRACT: every reorder PUT is an ABSOLUTE permutation computed from the order the caller can see. Two overlapping mutations therefore both compute a valid permutation from the same pre-mutation order, and whichever response lands last silently overwrites the other. Verified against the live pages: `run()` sets `busy` via React state (DownloaderPage.tsx:293-304, ConvertPage.tsx:354-365) which is asynchronous and is never consulted by `reorder()` (DownloaderPage.tsx:312-322), so nothing today serializes these paths. The module-level lifetime and the useQueueBulk ownership are forced by a direct read of ui/src/renderer/src/lib/queue/use-queue-bulk.ts:80-110 (the void-returning fold), re-verified 2026-09-03.
REORDER_SINGLE_FLIGHT_RULE.note: Added in plan review round 1 (F1); lifetime and bulk-fold ownership corrected in round 4 (R3-F1). The round-1 wording said 'each page holds one instance in a ref' and named the bulk fold without saying who acquires for it - two gaps the round-3 reviewer was right to reject: a ref does not survive unmount, and no page-level wrapper of a void-returning hook callback exists. ALT_ARROW_SUPPRESSION_RULE is NOT sufficient on its own: it only silences Alt+Arrow on the card that is locally dragging, and does nothing about an already in-flight keyboard/kebab/bulk PUT whose response lands after a drag PUT. Suppression handles the input-time collision; this gate handles the request-time race. Both ship. Proved by AC-49.31-49.35 and AC-49.37. Round-5 (R4-F3): the reactive surface is added because round 4 asserted a rendered consequence (AC-49.35, AC-49.38) of a state no component could observe. Round-6 (R5-F1): round 5 put the HOOK in this module too, which contradicted task row 4a's "the module is pure and has no React import" - one artifact forbade the very export another required, so following either one broke the other. The store/hook split resolves it in the direction that keeps the command layer React-free, and every artifact now names REORDER_HELD_HOOK for the binding and this rule for the store. Adding it here rather than in a page-local useState is deliberate: page-local state dies on unmount and reintroduces exactly the remount hole AC-49.37 exists to close.

VITEST_COLLECTION_FAILURE_SHAPE.value: In Vitest's --reporter=json output a MISSING MODULE and a MISSING NAMED EXPORT produce different shapes, and the Red oracle depends on the difference. (1) Missing module: collection for the whole file fails, the file's testResults entry has status=failed, assertionResults=[] and a non-empty top-level `message` naming the unresolved specifier; NONE of that file's tests are counted in numTotalTests. (2) Missing NAMED export from an existing module: the file COLLECTS and runs, `message` is empty, and the individual assertion fails normally with a populated failureMessages array. Consequence: appending a test that imports a not-yet-created module to an EXISTING green test file SUBTRACTS that file's passing tests from numTotalTests. (3) The `message` WORDING is not single-valued: two different layers report the same fact, and which one wins depends on how far the file got before the missing specifier was reached. Vite's import-analysis plugin says `Failed to resolve import "<specifier>" from "<file>". Does the file exist?` and the Node ESM loader says `Cannot find module '<specifier>' imported from '<absolute file>'`. Both name the specifier, which is the part clause (b2) actually needs; neither wording may be hard-coded. See VITEST_UNRESOLVED_MODULE_PATTERN.
VITEST_COLLECTION_FAILURE_SHAPE.source: Empirical measurement 2026-09-03 on this tree, not inference. Two throwaway probe specs were added under ui/tests/unit/ - one importing a nonexistent module, one importing a nonexistent named export from the existing download-controls module - and `npm --prefix ui run test -- --reporter=json` was captured to C:/Temp/av-kit/probe-collect.json. Result: numTotalTests=9, numTotalTestSuites=5, numFailedTestSuites=3; the missing-module file reported assertionResults=0 with the "Cannot find module" message, the missing-export file reported assertionResults=1 with an ordinary AssertionError and an empty message. Both probe files were deleted and their removal verified with `git status --porcelain -- ui/tests/unit/`. Clause (3) was measured later, on 2026-09-04, from the FIRST real Red-phase run of this MEU (C:/Temp/av-kit/meu49-red.json): in one single run reorder-body.test.ts reported the Vite import-analysis wording while reorder-single-flight.test.ts and queue-dnd.test.ts reported the Node loader wording, all three for statically imported, genuinely absent relative specifiers. That run is what falsified the round-4 assumption of one fixed wording.

VITEST_UNRESOLVED_MODULE_PATTERN.note: Added as execution-phase correction X2. RED_PHASE_ORACLE clause (b2) originally hard-coded the string 'Cannot find module', which made the oracle FAIL on a genuinely, correctly red suite - the strongest possible kind of oracle defect, because it punishes the exact state the Red phase is supposed to reach. Clause (b2) now matches this alternation for the KIND of failure and, independently, [regex]::Escape(<expected specifier>) for the IDENTITY of the missing module; the two checks are no longer chained through an elseif, so a wrong-module failure is still caught when the wording is the unexpected one. Widening the KIND check is safe precisely because the specifier check is what discriminates a typo'd import from an expected-absent one. Proven by assert-red-phase.ps1 -SelfTest case18.

REORDER_HELD_HOOK.value: NEW module `ui/src/renderer/src/lib/queue/use-queue-reorder-held.ts`, the ONLY React binding over REORDER_SINGLE_FLIGHT_RULE's store. It exports one hook: `useQueueReorderHeld(key: ReorderQueueKey): boolean`, implemented as `useSyncExternalStore((cb) => subscribeQueueReorder(key, cb), () => isQueueReorderHeld(key))`. `getSnapshot` returns a BOOLEAN, so it is referentially stable by construction and cannot trigger the "The result of getSnapshot should be cached" infinite-loop React throws for freshly-allocated snapshots. Because it reads the same module-level Map the acquire path writes, a component that unmounts and remounts re-subscribes to the LIVE gate state rather than to a fresh `false` - the same reason the registry is module-level at all (AC-49.37). QueueCard and QueueList import THIS module, never `useSyncExternalStore` directly, so there is exactly one subscription shape to reason about.
